The first time Miao Ying laid eyes on Fu Yuanshan, he was still a child who had already survived fifteen days alone amid the ruins left by Chaos's rampage. His wariness upon meeting Miao Ying was so intense that he nearly attacked her.\\nMiao Ying recognized the boy's potential and resolved to forge him into a spear to be hurled against the wastelands of Chaos.

Though Miao Ying took the boy in and named him Fu Yuanshan, she granted him no special favour. At fifteen, Fu Yuanshan joined the peasant cavalry, starting from the very bottom, but quickly showed remarkable skill in controlling horses — for he practically forced himself to live his life in the saddle.\\nThe young Fu Yuanshan believed that mankind's own strength alone could never match those monsters; only heavily armoured cavalry could smash the fiends head-on and achieve the vengeance he sought.

Fu Yuanshan's forces encountered a raiding party that Kairos Fateweaver had teleported across the Great Bastion by magic. Others proposed an immediate retreat, to regroup back at camp, but Fu Yuanshan knew well this was cowardice dressed as caution. He told them that unless they crushed the enemy before it could gain a foothold, they would surely be hunted down and slaughtered by the Chaos horde.\\nFu Yuanshan achieved an almost unbelievable victory, leading his cavalry in repeated sorties, lashing at the Chaos legion like a savage whip, before shattering the enemy formation in one brilliant cavalry charge and skewering the Chaos commander upon his own spear. The rest of the daemonic host scattered in flight.\\nBut Fu Yuanshan himself was gravely wounded by the enemy commander's counterattack, clinging to life by sheer force of will alone, when Miao Ying appeared before him. Had Fu Yuanshan fled during that battle, Miao Ying would never again have concerned herself with this mortal's fate — but Fu Yuanshan proved his hatred was strong enough, and his gift for war matched it. Miao Ying granted him her own blood, forging a Blood Dragon Descendant surpassing all others of his kind.

Once grown to manhood, Fu Yuanshan joined the Grand Dragon Horse cavalry, quickly rising through his own merit and even catching the eye of the great Nan Gau merchant Peng Du.\\nPeng Du wished to marry his daughter to Fu Yuanshan, offering a dowry that could have bought half of Nan Gau, but Fu Yuanshan refused, saying, 'While Chaos remains unswept, what use have I for a household?' This earned him the scorn of Nan Gau's merchants, and his comrades mocked his foolishness — but only Fu Yuanshan himself knew the true reason.\\nStill relying on his own skill, and through merit earned time and again by risking his life, Fu Yuanshan eventually rose to command the Grand Dragon Horse cavalry.\\nNow, with Cathay's mightiest force at his command, he waited patiently for his moment.

The Dragon Emperor's command arrived: Fu Yuanshan, as the most outstanding of the Blood Dragon Descendants, would command the eastern theatre of the Great Bastion, joining Miao Ying in the west to launch a campaign sweeping the Chaos forces north of the wall. But the strength of the Grand Dragon Horse alone would not suffice — this time, over a thousand Sky Junks would be dispatched, working alongside the Dragon Guard to complete the sweep.\\nFu Yuanshan met his new second-in-command: a snuff-snorting Cathayan Dwarf, who declared he would lend the wisdom of the Dwarfs to aid Fu Yuanshan's cause.

When the Cathayan army crossed the Great Bastion, a thousand Sky Junks blotted out the sun, and tens of thousands of Grand Dragon Horse cavalry unleashed their wings of death. The Chaos-tainted lands of the north, like a chronic plague, were swept clean. Kairos Fateweaver, too, was defeated by the combined might of Miao Ying and Zhao Ming, fleeing back into the Realm of Chaos amid the mocking laughter of Zhao Ming in his human form. Peace at last settled upon the borders of the Great Bastion.\\nStanding alongside the renown of the two living Dragon gods was Fu Yuanshan, a mere mortal whose achievements were no less than theirs. For this, he was reverently given the title Dragon General.\\nIn the years that followed, Fu Yuanshan never returned to Nan Gau, but spent his days, one after another, gazing across the distance at the Dragon Emperor's eldest daughter, together guarding the northern frontier of the Celestial Empire.

Chi Yan is the name of Fu Yuanshan's mount and closest companion in battle. This divine steed, hailing from the hills of Kun Lan, seems touched by some lingering essence of the Hao Tian Dragon Emperor born there — its head crowned with proud horns, thunder rippling along its back, hooves ablaze with wandering fire, its gallop swift as a falling star. Any foe who faces it head-on will feel a majesty rivaling that of a true dragon.

Fu Yuanshan, a war orphan taken in by Miao Ying, swore vengeance against the Chaos that slaughtered his entire family. Possessed of an unyielding will for revenge and extraordinary talent for war, he ultimately passed Miao Ying's trial and was granted the constitution of a Dragon Descendant through her secret art. From there, Fu Yuanshan rose step by step to command Cathay's armies, eventually marching north beyond the Great Bastion alongside Miao Ying and Zhao Ming to cleanse the Chaos-tainted lands that had long infested the north, bringing lasting peace to Cathay and completing his vengeance. Since then, Fu Yuanshan and Miao Ying have gazed upon each other from afar, together guarding Cathay's northern frontier. But at some point, unbeknownst even to himself, Fu Yuanshan found a shadow that would not leave his heart — a mere mortal, hopelessly yearning for the Dragon goddess he served beside.
